processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in Al2O3 crucibles using Fe with 99.99% purity (purified by zone melting to minimise impurity content) and Al with 99.999% purity.
Solidified in Cu moulds to obtain rods usually with 18 mm diameter; material used in the as-cast condition (no subsequent heat treatment).

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline Fe-18%Al with a coarse grain structure; as-cast alloys contained no second phases.

phases_present.phase_name: Fe-18%Al solid solution (disordered bcc alpha with short-range order / K-state)
phases_present.crystal_structure: bcc (disordered, with short-range order forming in the 13-18% Al range below 600 C after solidification)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Deformation twinning was observed for the Fe-18%Al alloy at both compression rates at room temperature; at -100 C twinning occurred above 14% Al in all specimens (occasionally for 11-14% Al). The room-temperature tensile curve of Fe-18at%Al shows a small load drop near 12% strain attributed to twinning.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Multiple slip in polycrystals; reduced dislocation mobility with increasing Al content; deformation twinning occurs for Fe-18%Al at room temperature because of insufficient dislocation mobility.
interfaces.interface_notes: Coarse-grained polycrystal with grain boundaries; the as-cast condition contains no second phases. Thin plate/rod-like carbides appear on grain boundaries only after slow furnace cooling from 1100 C or prolonged annealing, not in the as-cast state.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: 0.2% proof stress in compression with total straining of at least 5%

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Not reported for compression of Fe-18%Al as-cast; compression yield stress only.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Data obtained by averaging 3-4 tests (yield stress and strength data differed by 3% at most).

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fe-18at%Al RT tensile curve peaks just above the 500 MPa gridline with a small load drop near 12% strain (Fig. 4a).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: specimens etched by an alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution
characterization_methods.key_findings: Coarse grain structure of the order of 1 mm; as-cast Fe-18%Al contains no second phases.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, rates 10^-4 and 10^-2 s^-1, 0.2% proof stress
characterization_methods.purpose: determining the yield stress and its variation with Al content
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-18%Al yielded with concurrent twinning at both compression rates; elastic-limit yield stress lies just below 500 MPa.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rates between 10^-4 and 10^-2 s^-1, at room temperature and -100 C
characterization_methods.purpose: studying ductility (elongation before necking, fracture strain) and tensile strength
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-18at%Al shows highest strength and lowest fracture strain; brittle fracture without prior necking at RT; coarse serrations at -100 C due to deformation twinning.

characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis
characterization_methods.purpose: studying fracture surfaces and qualitative precipitate analysis

unmapped_findings: Real composition of the Fe-18%Al as-cast alloy (Table 1): nominal 18 at.%; real 17.5-18.0 at.% Al (9.3-9.6 wt.-%); impurities C 40-70 wt.ppm, Si <20-100 wt.ppm, As <70 wt.ppm, Ni <40 wt.ppm.

The yield stress of polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys increases linearly with Al content up to 18 at.% with a hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa (Fig. 3 and Fig. 5a,b), which is not sensitive to deformation rate or temperature; the interpolating straight lines in Fig. 3 indicate a yield stress increase of 21 and 23 MPa per unit % Al at the higher (10^-2 s^-1) and lower (10^-4 s^-1) compression rates, respectively.

The approximately 2.2 GPa hardening coefficient of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys contrasts with the ~1 GPa reported for monocrystals (single-slip) and ~1.8 GPa reported by Morgand et al. for polycrystals; the difference is attributed to alloy preparation (as-cast polycrystals vs annealed monocrystals) and slip mode (multiple vs single slip).

Deformation twinning was observed for the Fe-18%Al as-cast alloy at both compression rates at room temperature; at -100 °C twinning occurred above 14% Al in all specimens and occasionally for 11-14% Al.

Exceptional finding: the studied alloys show only minor effects of short-range ordering and no significant dependence of hardness on heat treatment (hardness data were obtained on Fe-16%Al monocrystals, not on this Fe-18% as-cast alloy).
Brittle fracture without prior necking occurs at room temperature for the as-cast alloy at 18 at.% Al (transition range 15-18 at.% Al at RT; 12-14 at.% Al at -100 °C).
